390.brief:
The market's heat is middling (+0.06 on a scale from −1 washed out to +1 stretched), so the plan keeps about half the money in cash: 50% invested, 50% in cash. The index is hot (S&P +0.81, Nasdaq +0.86), but the average stock is not (equal-weight +0.18, small caps -0.13): the biggest names carry the tape. 2 of 11 sectors lead (Technology, Energy), 5 lag, 3 turning up from below (Industrials, Utilities, Consumer discretionary), 1 pulling back (Health care). Read beside them, not counted in: Crypto +0.49, Metals -0.29. Inside the sectors the bow tie reads -0.17: the big names carry each sector. Across the 318 served names the advance/decline line fell 216 over the last 20 sessions (today 221 up, 91 down), and 73% of the set's move came from its ten largest names. Rates are a headwind at 5.27%. Volatility is calm (VIX 15.0).

The sectors are read by one blended bow tie — five readings per sector, averaged. The rung for a middling market is 50% invested, 50% cash. You hold 0% invested, so 50% of equity is to deploy, spread by each sector's own coldness — the biggest shares go to Consumer discretionary 7%, Utilities 6%, Industrials 6%, Real estate 4% of equity (the full split is in 3b · HOW THE MONEY SPLITS).

Inside those sectors the names that rank first — fundamentals first, then the Geiger for timing — are WDC (Technology, cheap vs peers, target +48%), GOOG (Communications, cheap vs peers, target +19%), GOOGL (Communications, in line vs peers, target +21%), NVDA (Technology, cheap vs peers, target +34%), TSM (Technology, cheap vs peers, target +12%). The knockout inside a cohort is section 5; their comparables and the checked analyst targets are in 8b.
